voluntary ingestion of a carbohydrate-electrolysate solution (CES) during gym-based exercise resulted in more adequate fluid balance and better maintenance of affect during exercise compared with water (W).

the ingestion of a carbohydrate-electroylete beverage (CES) compared to water or no fluids (NF) during gymnasium based exercise resulted in a greater voluntary intake of fluid, more adequate hydration and better maintenance of affect.

a carbohydrate-electrolysate solution was consumed in greater volumes than water and resulted in a greater maintenance of hydration, plasma glucose concentrations and affective states than water during exercise.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of voluntary fluid intake in maintaining fluid balance during exercise in a real-life setting and the effect of drink composition on fluid intake and affective states.
the effects of voluntary drinking behaviour, fluid intake, fluid balance, and affective states when exercising in a gym environment.
the role of voluntary intake of water and/or sports drinks on hydration status and affective states in physically active adults during gymnasium based exercise.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a CES is more effective in maintaining hydration status and affective state during gymnasium-type exercise than water.

the consumption of a carbohydrate-electroleyte solution (CES), compared to water (W) and no fluid intake (NF), results in more adequate hydration status and better maintenance of affect during exercise.

the ingestion of a CES, compared to water, during gymnasium based exercise, resulted in more fluid intake, more adequate hydration status, higher plasma glucose levels, and a better maintenance in affective states.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ingestion of a carbohydrate-electrolys drink (CES) is a better option for maintaining fluid balance than water during gymnasium based exercise.
the addition of carbohydrate and electrolytes to water can increase voluntary drinking during exercise and improve hydration status and affective states.
the addition of carbohydrate and electrolytes in a sports drink is beneficial to the athlete in a variety of ways.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the addition of a carbohydrate-electroleyte solution can improve the maintenance of hydration status, as well as the affective state, during exercise.
when given the opportunity, individuals prefer to consume a carbohydrate-electro-lyte beverage over plain water.
the addition of electrolytes to a carbohydrate solution may enhance the voluntary intake of a drink during exercise and maintain a more positive affective state.
